Lydia: By Dibella's tits, this piss-pot of a tavern reeks like a Thalmor whorehouse after a bad orgy—skeevers and shadows everywhere. You the one they call Delvin?

**Late visual context as seen by MJR (the player): MJR stands in a dimly lit cavernous space with rough stone walls arched overhead, supported by wooden beams that creak under the weight of the earth. Flickering torchlight casts long shadows across the uneven stone floor, revealing scattered wooden crates, barrels, and a makeshift ramp leading up to a higher ledge cluttered with more supplies. In the corner, a weathered man with a bald head and a thick beard sits hunched on a rough stool near a small wooden table, his face etched with fatigue as he stares into the dimness. Faded graffiti or markings on the wall nearby spell out "Dren's Den," and the air feels stale, heavy with the scent of damp earth and unwashed linens from a nearby pallet bed. A narrow tunnel entrance yawns to one side, partially obscured by hanging roots and debris.**

Lydia: Heard you're neck-deep in this rat-fuck guild, stealing from honest Nords while elves laugh from their towers. Delvin Mallory: Aye, that's me, love—Delvin Mallory, and this here's the heart of Riften's underbelly, not some elf's tea party.
Continue the conversation naturally.

Delvin Mallory: Aye, that's me, love—Delvin Mallory, at your service in this shithole we call home. And you? Struttin' in here like you own the damn Ratway, tits bustin' out of that getup like a Stormcloak wet dream. What brings a Nord firebrand like you to the Flagon at this unholy hour?
Continue the conversation naturally.

Delvin Mallory: Shor’s bones, lass, you stroll in here buck-naked like you own the damn Flagon? Guild’s seen worse than a fine Nord rack at four in the mornin’, but you’re makin’ my old eyes water—pass the mead afore I forget I’m workin’. Lydia: Eyes up here, you bald rat-bastard, or I’ll shove that dagger where the sun don’t shine. This skin’s for my Thane’s blade alone, not your greasy guild of cutpurse scum hidin’ in Dibella’s shadows like Thalmor spies.
Continue the conversation naturally.

Lydia: The name's Lydia, housecarl to the Dragonborn himself—MJR, the arrow-slinging bastard who's got more kills than you've got sticky fingers. We're sloggin' through this Dibella-forsaken sewer at four in the mornin' to shake down some leads on them bandit sluts huntin' my Thane like he's a prize hog. You got any dirt on elf-lovin' whores lurkin' in Riften, or you just sit here jerkin' off to your shadowmarks?
Continue the conversation naturally.

Delvin Mallory: Ha! Easy there, warrior-princess—ain't no Thalmor spy, just a fella who's dodged more blades than you've split skulls in this damp rat-maze. Four bells past midnight, and the Flagon's quieter than a skeever's fart;

**Late visual context as seen by MJR (the player): From MJR's vantage point, the scene unfolds in a dimly lit underground chamber with high, vaulted ceilings of rough-hewn brick arches that curve overhead, casting long shadows in the flickering torchlight. The walls are uneven stone, mottled with age and dampness, supported by sturdy wooden beams that creak faintly under the weight of the earth above. A narrow wooden bridge stretches across a shallow chasm or trench, its planks weathered and splintered, flanked by simple railings of lashed timber. On the stone floor below, scattered with loose gravel and puddles, stands a group of figures huddled near a makeshift wooden barricade. To the right, a woman with long, flowing hair and minimal attire—barely more than scraps of fabric clinging to her form—leans against the railing, her posture relaxed yet alert, a small dagger visible at her hip. Nearby, two other shadowy silhouettes, cloaked and armored, murmur among themselves, their faces partially obscured by hoods. The air feels heavy with the scent of earth and smoke, and faint echoes suggest deeper tunnels branching off into darkness beyond the bridge.**

Delvin Mallory: what's a loyal housecarl like you doin' pokin' around our shadows instead of guardin' your Thane's arse from those bandit sluts? Lydia: Guardin' it from scum like you, more like—heard your guild's finger-deep in every Imperial pocket from here to Solitude, lettin' elves and orcs bleed Skyrim dry while honest Nords like my MJR fight the real war.
Continue the conversation naturally.

Delvin Mallory: Bandit sluts, eh? Riften's crawlin' with 'em at this witchin' hour—four bells past midnight, and the Ratway's thicker than Vex's ass with desperate cunts sniffin' for coin or cock. Heard whispers from my fences 'bout a pack o' tattooed whores holed up near the docks, eyein' highborn targets like your Dragonborn prick. They ain't elf-lovers, though—more like Kahjiit-cum dumpsters tradin' flesh for skooma.
Please wrap up the current topic between the NPCs in a natural way. Nobody is leaving, so there is no need for formal goodbyes.

Delvin Mallory: ... bandit sluts? You mean them curvy cutthroats raidin' from the shadows like ghosts with a grudge? Flagon's seen a few slip through the Ratway bridges—hooded bastards murmurkin' by the barricades over that piss-trench below, waitin' for fools like us at this dead hour. But dirt on elves? Oi, watch that Nord fire, lass—Guild's got no love for them elf pricks or orc hordes any more than you do; we're the ones slippin' daggers into their backs while Stormcloaks grandstand up top. But bandit sluts raidin' for your Thane? Spill more—might know a mark or two in this four-AM fog down here, if it lines our pockets.

Delvin Mallory: Look, love, I ain't sayin' we don't got our fingers in a few pies, but these tattooed bitches?

Delvin Mallory: They're runnin' with some skooma cartel out by the docks—nasty cunts tradin' flesh for highs, always sniffin' for fresh meat like your Thane.

Vex: I see you lot made a mess in the Ratway. Gian the Fist won't be collecting any more debts, I take it. Delvin Mallory: About damn time someone put that brute down. He's been shaking down our fence contacts for weeks. Bad for business. Lydia: He threatened my Thane. No one threatens MJR and lives to brag about it. Vex: Well, you've done us a favor. Gian was getting too bold, thinking he could muscle in on Guild territory. Mercer will be pleased. Delvin Mallory: Speaking of Mercer - the Guild's been lying low since that whole mess with the Goldenglow Estate went sideways. You're not here to cause more trouble, are you? Lydia: We're just passing through Riften on our way to Ivarstead. Jarl Balgruuf has business for my Thane in the Rift. Vex: The Jarl of Whiterun sending his thane into our little corner of Skyrim? That's unusual. What's a woman like you doing mixed up with politics anyway? Lydia: I serve MJR, not politics.

Vex: Brynjolf, you old charmer. Trying to recruit another fresh face into the Guild, are you? Delvin Mallory: Ha! That one's got coin written all over him. Look at that armor - top quality. Let me guess, you're here to offload some hot merchandise? Lydia: My Thane is no common fence. We're on important business from Whiterun. Though I suppose your lot wouldn't understand honor and duty. Vex: Honor and duty don't fill coin purses, Nord. Tell me, does your Thane have a steady hand with a lockpick, or is he all brawn like his housecarl? Lydia: MJR's archery could put an arrow through your eye before you even drew that dagger of yours. I've seen him drop bandits at three hundred paces.

Vex: An old man hiding in the Warrens, paying the Guild for secrecy? That sounds like someone with either a lot of coin or a lot of enemies. Delvin Mallory: Either way, it's good business. We don't ask questions when the gold's right. But if your Thane is planning to pay him a visit, tell him to watch his step down there. The Warrens make the rest of the Ratway look like the Blue Palace. Lydia: My Thane can handle himself better than any skulking shadow in these sewers. We've faced dragons and vampires - a few rats won't be a problem. Vex: Confidence. I like it.

Vex: Quiet night in the Flagon. Almost peaceful, for a den of thieves. Delvin Mallory: Peaceful means light purses. I'd rather have some action, keeps the coin flowing. Speaking of which, that one over there - Galathil - she's been eyeing your Thane since he walked in. Lydia: Hmph. A flesh sculptor. I've heard tales of their work. Seems unnatural to me, carving up a face like clay. A Nord earns their scars with honor. Vex: Not all of us want to look like we've been in a bar brawl every day of our lives. Some prefer a more... refined appearance.

Vex: You know, Delvin, with Gian dead and the heat dying down, we might actually get some proper work coming in again. That disruption was hurting our take from the docks. Delvin Mallory: Aye, the boys from the fishery were getting nervous with him shaking down their shipments. Might be time to send a message that the Guild's still the only game in town for protection. Lydia: Protection. That's a fancy word for extortion.

Vex: Call it what you will, Nord. But without the Guild, Riften would be overrun with cutthroats who have no code. We keep the peace down here. Delvin Mallory: What my charming colleague means is that we provide a service. Merchants pay for safety, and they get it. Everyone wins. Lydia: protection
Vex: You Nords and your honor.

(Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Daegon, Serana, Sapphire, Vipir the Fleet, Etienne Rarnis) (MJR: What's missing from the vault?; Brynjolf: Better question would be "what did he leave?" Mercer took everything. Even all of our plans are gone.) (MJR: Plans for what?; Brynjolf: Before Mercer took over, Gallus started collecting every bit of material he could on locations the Guild could heist. Museums, keeps, estates... you name it. By the time Mercer took over the Guild we must have had a few dozen.) (MJR: How could he have opened the vault door alone?; Brynjolf: I don't have a clue. That door is impenetrable. Without two keys, it's impossible to open. I have a key, Delvin has a key, and Mercer has a key. That's it. There are no other copies.) (MJR: What's the best way to get into Riftweald Manor?; Brynjolf: Good question. I've only set foot inside a few times myself and that was in Mercer's company. If you can get past his trained watchdog, I think your best bet might be the ramp to the second floor balcony in his backyard.) (MJR: I don't suppose the ramp is easy to access.; Brynjolf: No. It's some sort of crazy contraption Mercer commissioned for quick escapes. I'd wager a well-placed shot at the ramp's mechanism would lower it in a hurry.) (MJR: You mentioned a watchdog?; Brynjolf: Hmph. That'd be Vald. A real piece of work, that one. Mercer's holding something over his head, keeping him loyal. Talk to Vex. She used to know him very well... if you catch my meaning.) (The location is now The Ragged Flagon.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Vex, Daegon, Serana, Lydia, Galathil) (MJR: I heard you're offering extra work.; Vex: I handle the burglary, shill, sweep, and heist jobs. Most of them involve breaking and entering. If you don't like that kind of work, talk to Delvin. He runs the more up close and personal jobs.) (MJR: Brynjolf sent me.; Tonilia: So, you're the new recruit, huh? Well, looks like you and I are going to have to get very well acquainted. MJR: Why is that?; Tonilia: I'm the fence down here. You come by anything you don't exactly own and I'll pay you some coin for it. Minus a little slice for the Guild, of course. I can also provide a few supplies useful to our trade now and again, for a small fee. MJR: Is there anything you don't charge for?; Tonilia: Sure, how about I get Dirge to knock you over your head and dump you into the cistern? Look, I've been in this business a long time and I've seen all types. You can play it tough, or you can play it smart... whatever. At the end of the day, you'll find that all we care about down here is how much gold you can make us. MJR: Understood.; Tonilia: Good. Then there isn't much more to say. Here's your armor, just make sure you put it to good use. MJR: ...; Tonilia: Well, looks like you're fitting in well down here. I'm supposed to allow you to trade in one of your pieces of Guild armor, so what will it be? MJR: Anything different about it?; Tonilia: Of course... otherwise it wouldn't be much of a reward, now would it? Your new piece will enhance your skill beyond that of the original. Trust me. MJR: I'll trade in my boots.; Tonilia: Are you sure? Once I exchange it for you, I'm not taking it back... unless you want to sell it at a discount of course. MJR: Yes, I'm sure.; Tonilia: Okay, there you go.)

Delvin Mallory: Two in the morning and the place is still buzzing like a hive of anxious bees. Mercer's betrayal has everyone on edge. Vekel the Man: Aye, and my mead sales have doubled. Misery loves company, and cheap drink. Tonilia: Vekel, you'd sell your own mother's tears if you could bottle them. But Delvin's right. That vault being empty changes everything for us. Delvin Mallory: Empty isn't quite the word I'd use. Cleaned out like a Nord's plate after a feast. Gallus spent years building those plans, and Mercer just... walked off with them. Vekel the Man: Walked off with a key that was supposed to be impossible to copy. Brynjolf's been pacing for hours trying to figure it out. Tonilia: I've seen Mercer charm his way through plenty of locked doors. That man had more tricks than a mages' college dropout. But this... this is different. He planned this for a long time. Delvin Mallory: The question is whether he planned it alone. Someone had to help him get into that vault without the rest of us knowing.
